rows.text: Don't be too mad. I wasn't a Stellaron Hunter back then, but wasn't everything that happened in Penacony the perfect opportunity to join?
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What did you do to Firefly?
Though it wasn't my original intention, I wanted to help her, to keep her from getting caught up in Gopher Wood's schemes and facing such a detestable fate.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Alas, I couldn't make it happen. The path your predecessor Razalina left in the memoria pushed Firefly towards a {RUBY_B#dead end}new lease on life{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Indeed, how could a Nameless who walks the path of the Trailblaze leave behind a legacy built on "evading destiny"?
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What's the deal with the Dreammaster?
As you can see, he became a martyr, leaving all his power in the Twelve Hours, like a self-turning hand of time, driving his plans forward.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The Order truly is a harsh Path. Ena, Gopher Wood, and Sunday, the one you know even better... They all chose to sacrifice themselves for it.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But then, something interesting happened: You turned out to be that "variable."
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: As Aventurine said, Razalina's legacy would send dreamers to where they truly yearned to be. For Firefly, that place turned out to be by your side.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: She revealed her true self to you, reuniting with you as a Stellaron Hunter.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Then, guided by a History Fictionologist, you witnessed the life of the Watchmaker Mikhail.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: It was truly a life worth remembering, worth giving everything for. I would've loved to raise a glass of "Hello and Goodbye" to him, just like the one who saw things through to the end, Mr. Gallagher. What a shame I can't do it properly here.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Sunday also came here, feigning cooperation, to reveal to you the truth about Penacony. The foundation of the sweet dream, hidden behind the Grand Theater's curtain, was actually a Stellaron, and the true mastermind behind everything was none other than the Dreammaster Gopher Wood.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But you know now that his words weren't entirely true. What followed was one of the few beautiful memories that Firefly has held onto to this day...
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: In order to win tickets to the Grand Theater, you and Firefly participated in the Moment of Scorchsand auditions. Your coordination was so perfect, like you were companions who'd long shared the same rhythm.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: See? Even though you've forgotten everything from before, some traces remain etched in this moment, becoming part of your instincts.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Until... following the "script," Firefly sent you all to the final stage before departing on her own. In those beautiful moments before that, she experienced the joy of living, yet she still had to... face the terror of death.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: However, you may have noticed that during this period there was a small gap. She and you weren't together the whole time.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: You returned to a child's dream through a dream bubble left by Mikhail and witnessed his {RUBY_B#Trailblaze}legacy{RUBY_E#}. However, Firefly was not a Trailblazer, so she couldn't enter it.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: While waiting alone, she met her true collaborator... and thus learned that there was more than one legacy in Penacony, and more than one Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Ignore that. Must be some meme. How did it end up here?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Sorry, I want to go check that out real quick. Be right back.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Oh? So you're into "fluffies" too? You've got taste! Better not wander too far though.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: What does the Dreammaster gain from recreating the Swarm Disaster?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Hah...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You're quite familiar with memoria, so you should be able to tell whether this memory is fabricated or not.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Laying the foundation for "Eternal Paradise?" This...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: At that time, she was trying to escape her own destiny.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But when the Swarm was discovered on Penacony, she didn't just stand idly by. Even though she died while fighting against the Swarm, it wasn't destiny catching up with her again.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It was her own choice, because like any ordinary person, she had a conscience and knew compassion.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Is she your friend?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Yes... And in many moments, looking at her is like seeing myself.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I know it won't undo what's been done, but... I'm sorry. No matter what purpose the Dreammaster has, it doesn't give him the right to sacrifice anyone.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I promise you, when all of this is over, regardless of the outcome, I'll tell everyone about her deeds. She deserves to be remembered by the sweet dream.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Reminds me of the good old days during the War of Gods...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But there's one thing I don't understand. Even if the Dreammaster is after the power of the Propagation, there are plenty of Swarms left in the cosmos. Why resort to killing?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's exactly why we came to find you.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: With the Charmony Festival about to begin, it can't be a mere coincidence that the Dreammaster is pushing forward with his various machinations now, and you were chosen to perform for the Harmony. Whether you're aware of it or not, you must be absolutely crucial to his plans.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I see...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Oh, silly me, I almost forgot — I need to retrieve a certain {RUBY_B#"Jade" Cornerstone}lost item{RUBY_E#}. Otherwise, there's a lady who won't be too pleased.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Sorry, but I need to get going.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Sorry, but you're not going anywhere.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: This is the land chosen by Gopher Wood to "meet disaster," but he doesn't want the Swarm to truly surge forth and devour the world.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: ...The Swarm Disaster will be trapped here, and so will you in your weakened state.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Unless a kind Memokeeper lends a helping hand, right?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But I can't find a reason. So far, there hasn't been a single case of one of the Ten Stonehearts being killed. It's driving me crazy with curiosity!
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Whose backup is this?
rows.speaker: Aventurine & The Dahlia

rows.text: Pardon my late introduction. I am Argenti of the Knights of Beauty, traversing the cosmos to eradicate all that is unsightly in this world.
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: In the name of Beauty, the One and Only has brought me to this place. Perhaps it is destiny's guidance that led me here. In this dreamscape tainted by the Propagation, I shall uphold the name of Beauty and clear the path for all of you!
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: ...Ah, passing knight, you've found just the right person. I am an IPC envoy trapped here. Lend me your aid, for Idrila the Beauty is the most peerless beauty of them all!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Someone's a quick learner...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Nothing else to say? This is far too much of a coincidence.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: What else is there to say? Would this Sir Knight even listen to us try to reason with him?
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: That's the fascinating thing about destiny. Some people are just born lucky. Let them be. We should get moving now.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: ...Where are we going?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: To find your dance partner, darling. By an unexpected turn of events, the Dreammaster's plan is about to come to fruition, and to deal with him...
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: ...We'll need an Emanator to step in.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Since the future of the Stellaron, Penacony, and even the entire Cosmos is at stake, let's draw a conclusion there, in all fairness.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Does that mean he wants to fight us during the Charmony Festival?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm afraid so.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Anyway, we can't leave the Stellaron unchecked. This is about Trailblazing a bright future for Penacony and fulfilling the long-cherished wishes of Mikhail and our other predecessors.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Is this the place...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Where the Dreammaster executes all his schemes?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Or perhaps, it's the place where he'll find redemption.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster" Gopher Wood (?)

rows.text: ...Dreammaster!?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: No... just one of his "divine laws".
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster" Gopher Wood (?)

rows.text: Don't think I'll let my guard down. I know your true nature. Whatever your goal is, I will stop you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: No need to be so tense, Miss Firefly. I am but a thought formed from memory. Feel free to strike me if you wish to verify this.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: But his actions aren't baseless. There's a reason for my presence here.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...Please continue.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Thank you for your openness.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I'm equally unaware of the Dreammaster's malicious plans, but he's been waiting for your arrival. That Glamoth Knight he killed with his own hands... through me, he hopes to restore "justice" for her. And you, her friend, are meant to witness it.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...Justice?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Indeed. I'm quite familiar with this place and can guide you. This has its own significance for you, too. Witnessing his confession is tantamount to unveiling his crimes.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I don't need your guidance to get this done.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But you need someone to decipher the truth. Force alone won't solve anything.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: It's not like you'll stop here if I refuse. Lead the way, but I'll be keeping my eye on you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What is this place?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Oak Manor, once part of the Dewlight Pavilion. Before becoming the Dreammaster, he used to hold family councils here, but it's been abandoned for years now, sinking into the Primordial Memory Zone.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I'm afraid it's... pain.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Did Oak Manor always have decor like this?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: After taking over the sweet dream, {RUBY_B#Gopher Wood}he{RUBY_E#} never turned away any sincere dream seekers, even if they were shady characters.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Walking along the Harmony, he firmly believed that even villains could be transformed by Xipe's benevolence. To show mercy, act with justice, and walk with humility.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: It seems his wishes didn't come true.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Indeed, those villains never learned their lesson. They even conspired with one another, foolishly attempting to establish their own family lineage. Such arrogance! They went as far as sending a messenger across the vast cosmos to seek permission from the Main Family.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: In the end, they only brought shame upon themselves.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: And then there was a revolt?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Fortunately, his heart was already aligned with the Oak Family, allowing him to survive by sheer luck... though he could never leave the sweet dream again.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Soon after, the manor was decorated this way.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Was he trying to warn himself?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: If your beliefs lead you down a path of plight, why stubbornly cling to them?
rows.speaker: "Who is Imprisoned in Dreams"

rows.text: ...That's exactly what I'm getting at.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: At least now... I can understand those feelings.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And I think I've come to understand why I exist here.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: At that moment, Gopher Wood stood at a crossroads, pondering whether the Harmony was still the right path. But my fragmented memories have not yet revealed where this would ultimately lead...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Since he was about to commit a great evil, perhaps the Dreammaster who left behind these laws was hoping I would choose a different path.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: But it's too late to change anything now.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Not necessarily. We might as well keep moving forward. Good intentions are always the final creation of evil deeds, for they know they must be stopped. And his past choices will reveal his schemes to us.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: In your opinion, which path would the Dreammaster choose?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Probably the path of "force." But Miss Firefly, feel free to do as you please. I have no other thoughts today.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: The road not taken can never be retraced. Even in dreams, this truth remains...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I barely escaped death, and I still can't reveal my true form. Tell me, why have I been branded a criminal upon returning to this place?
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: You've already confessed to your crimes.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: The Family doesn't tolerate incompetence, even from a branch leader on the frontier. Not only did this one fail to quell the situation, he was even murdered. If it weren't for Nanook's manifestation, the Eternal Centurion would have descended upon Penacony to eliminate these villains.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: But you survived by sheer luck, and I set out for this very reason. You must settle this matter yourself and reclaim your lost respect... not for yourself, but for The Family.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: ...To survive, but without the power to do anything.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Therefore, your crime shall be punished with a "blessing"...
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: I shall bestow upon you another crime. Its evil reaches even the heavens, and once known, the name Gopher Wood will lose all meaning. You will be alive in body but dead in spirit.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: I know my sins. Please bestow your punishment.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Here and now? That's not possible. Before I lead you to that honeyed fountain, I shall tune you so that you can no longer speak out.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: People believe it to be a creation of the Destruction, for it always arrives coupled with calamity.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: I shall clear the shadows before your eyes, so that you may once again behold that almighty force that giveth and taketh, and worship the mercy bestowed by the Triple Face...
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: The {RUBY_B#Xipe's}Harmonic{RUBY_E#} Cancer, the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: "Family's Envoy, Awoken Mode"

rows.text: Did the Dreammaster already know back then that the Stellaron was actually a creation of the Path of Harmony... Was he forced to manipulate the Stellaron under The Family's orders?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'd like to defend him, but calling it "forced" would be self-deception...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: He claimed he was "powerless," not that "Xipe taught us we shouldn't do this." Whatever The Family's true face may be, right now, Gopher Wood is no longer a follower of the Harmony.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: What if you were the one standing there?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Perhaps I too would betray the Harmony. But in any case, that would only mean I found The Family unworthy of obedience. It doesn't justify the Dreammaster's heinous acts.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...Miss Firefly, have you ever pondered over destiny?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I often wonder, if we could face our past decisions again, would we really make different choices?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: It's in that puppet's hand, Lady Firefly.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Got it.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Rest in peace now, old friend.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Mikhail... Was it you who killed him?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Is that what you think of the Dreammaster? Someone so unforgivably evil?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: He was once the Dreammaster's closest friend, but they ultimately parted ways due to their differences over the sweet dream. Mikhail once gave the Dreammaster a wristwatch, and even though it's broken now, he still treasures it to this day.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I came for a "confession," old friend. I wonder... what did death feel like to you...
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: I died once, yet returned to the mortal realm. If you were as fortunate as I was, would we still walk different paths?
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: ...In my eyes, you can still hold onto hope precisely because you've never faced inevitable death.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Would you blame me? Would you, Mikhail?
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: I tried to unveil Xipe's third face, but I was wrong. It wasn't the Propagation. Yet destiny was so merciful, making me realize...
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: The Propagation was able to continuously evoke people's prayers for the Order through the fear brought by the Swarm. When the Swarm Disaster ravaged the universe, that was also when the Order reached its unprecedented peak.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: But after that, {RUBY_B#Ena}the Great One{RUBY_E#} deliberately ignited a war among gods, leading to THEIR own downfall. THEY would rather fall than let the Order ascend upon a staircase of falsehoods.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: THEY were wrong too.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: The Great One wished to restore justice to the mortal world, but what people prayed for wasn't justice. It was "freedom from fear."
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Will you forgive me? Will you, Mikhail?
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: I shall commit an act of transgression, mending the errors of the gods. I will restore the missing {RUBY_B#fear}hand{RUBY_E#} to the celestial clock and show mankind death.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: I know my sins. They are ever before me. But I shall never repent.
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Using the Propagation to lay the foundation for an eternal paradise... So what he meant was...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Recreate the Swarm Disaster, using fear to force people to... pray for the Order's return?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Perhaps that's why your friend was killed. The Dreammaster wanted to find out how the Glamoth Iron Cavalry obtained the Propagation's power.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: That's not a power that can be easily controlled. We need to pick up the pace.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Past this point lies the grand hall at the end of Oak Manor.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: And before us lies his final decision: where to go after turning away from the Harmony.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Since he wants you to choose again, which side will you take?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Go ahead with whichever path you think is right. I'll take the other one.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Don't worry, I can't change anything. Even if I have a sudden awakening, it would only give the Dreammaster peace of mind.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: He deserves absolute punishment, and must be brought to heel.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: So you made a different choice after all.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I will stop him.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: "The impossible in dreams is not 'Death,' but 'Dormancy.' Do stay alive. I wish you the best of luck."
I hope everything goes well. This is goodbye then.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Déjà vu... I can smell the "resentment" lingering in this place.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: So many... Could Gopher Wood's plan already be in motion?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: No... Impossible...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: This place already looks... We need to hurry.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What a desolate sight...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Nothing seems out of place... Did I pick the wrong one?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: If I were to have no choice
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: Nor shall you
rows.speaker: Dreammaster Gopher Wood

rows.text: No doubt about it, this is the place.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: My apologies for keeping you waiting, Lady Firefly.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Ah, it's you. It seems the other path leads here too.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What is this?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It's the terror that humanity dares not recall: the Swarm Disaster's Chrysalis of Extinction.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: The Dreammaster's devastating strike, like a torrent of fire, lies hidden behind the stained glass, waiting to shatter it and unleash the Swarm Disaster once again.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...How did the Dreammaster become this powerful?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: We need to stop him.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Or maybe... stop me.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: (As expected...)
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I shall end this matter on his behalf. This thought, together with the power beyond the window, completes a single, true "divine law."
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...Divine law?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Everything you saw along the way, none of that was meant for you. It was meant for me, so that I could bring you justice.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: ...I don't see any justice in any of this.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Lady Firefly, I assume you've pondered over destiny too?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I don't think it can be used as an excuse for anything.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Even if the ending is predetermined, we can still decide how we get there.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's just self-deception. You've never been able to change the course of events.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: When we stand at the crossroads of choice, no matter how many times we start over, we'll always make the same decision. By that moment in time, we've already been shaped by our past, believing that choice to be the only correct path.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: All the past you've left behind has already determined your future.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Your friend tried to escape destiny, only to meet the same end. And now, here you are, no different.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: But the person you met today is someone who has rewritten their destiny.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Well then, I'll offer you my sympathy, Hunter. As far as I know, there's only one way to rewrite destiny.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Give up your true desires and stop walking your own path. In doing so, your destiny will indeed change, and you may even sway the course of the world.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: But from that moment on, you will have killed yourself... alive in body, but dead in spirit.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: This is the price we're willing to pay to defy destiny. Not everyone chooses to surrender with their hands up.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: "Everyone has the power to see the world as it is, and to bear that weight. This is the true meaning of {RUBY_B#resistance}sacrifice{RUBY_E#}."
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I admire your resolve. Since you don't mind sacrifice...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: That's enough talk. Stand down, Hunter. You can't stop that strike.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I won't let you get away with this.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Oh really? How did the Harmony succeed in spreading its {RUBY_B#Stellarons}cancer{RUBY_E#} across the universe then?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Though she wasn't my true companion, that Cremator left me with a spark of her flame.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I never trusted you. During our journey together, I planted it on you, and now, I'll let it reignite. It can burn away a thread of thought with ease.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: "11:30█Repent and return to righteousness. Though you soar like an eagle and make your nest among the stars, I will bring you down from there."
Impressive, but do you really think you can get ahead of me?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: If I can't, I still won't run away. If that strike is inevitable, I'll be the only one who dies in this nightmare.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Your courage shines like pure gold. Even so...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: "11:45█Paradise shall fall into this world of sorrow, and once dawn breaks, it will shatter in the light of day. How could anything golden abide in glory forever?"
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Come forth and present yourself, last heir of the Empire. I permit you to unveil the true face of Order...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: I permit you, with mortal hands, to bring forth {RUBY_B#Ena}the Great One{RUBY_E#}!
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (III)"

rows.text: Your last confession took me by surprise.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Mr. Gopher Wood, no... the Final Divine Law.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I suspect there was never any Chrysalis of Extinction from the Swarm Disaster to begin with, was there?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What exists in Oak Manor is nothing but a disguise. The only thing hidden within is a Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: True, I never unraveled the secrets of the Propagation. Now split into four parts, a single strike of mine cannot harm that Hunter.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: But if a pathstrider of the same origin as the Swarm were to be deceived by tuning, mistaking what lies before them as certain death... If they were to make a wish "to live" before the Stellaron... The outcome would twist into a catastrophe that brings death: the Swarm Disaster.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Her life shall "beget death," and that death shall "beget life" unto this world. But why are you so certain that nothing will go wrong?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I've already glimpsed the secrets of the Stellaron, and I have no need for certainty here. Even if she never entered the game, that strike would still fall at the appointed time, causing the Stellaron to shatter.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: The dreamers will learn that the power to destroy their own lives comes from the Harmony, but that it is ultimately the worst option.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: You should know that I won't agree with this.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Too late, child. The hands of time have struck midnight. Look up at the stars. Do you know why they are so cruel?
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: That reason shall be the final "divine law." And with this, we entrust everything into your hands...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: "00:00█Because the stars belong to everyone, they have never belonged to anyone. If you love everyone, then you love no one."
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: Well, that's where our conversation ends. Go ahead. The 107,336 souls of the Oak Family have dreamed of this moment too many times...
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: The opening is near. Go, my child. Seize the power of the Harmony and reveal your karma.
rows.speaker: "Divine Law (IV): Midnight"

rows.text: I shall walk the path of the Order to its end, as you wish. But I can no longer accept your divine laws. If I become {RUBY_B#the flawless sun}the only star{RUBY_E#} in the sky, even if I belonged to no one, there would still be no cruelty.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The stars are cruel, only because they have never shared their heat with the masses, burning fiercely only for themselves.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Well, there can't be two suns in the sky. I'll step up and take down the other sun if necessary.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Moreover, how could I allow other stars to shine during the day?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Paradise shall soon be created, not at midnight, but at "noon." I shall initiate the first and only divine law of the Great Septimus...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "12:00█I shall ascend to the heavens, becoming the scorching sun. Bathed in my light, my people shall flourish, while all evil shall be eradicated."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Very well, child... do what you must. Perhaps I was never truly without a path, but too devoted to choosing what was safest. Even if it proves impossible, I will still see it through.
rows.speaker: "Fading Last Words"

rows.text: I should become a Watchmaker too. The harmony I seek has but one note repeating endlessly, never falling out of tune...
rows.speaker: "Fading Last Words"

rows.text: Life, too, has its time.
rows.speaker: "Fading Last Words"

rows.text: Dreamflux Reef, Mikhail's will hence flows into tomorrow...
Did they enter that dream bubble?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's right. Unfortunately, you won't be able to follow them in so easily, even if you've traveled together as companions.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: That old man can be so stubborn sometimes... He'd rather have the Nameless be the ones to witness his legacy.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: No, I think it's quite romantic.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: A legacy left in the past will give them the courage to continue walking towards the future. Even if I can't walk alongside them, I'm content in knowing this.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Hah. You're quite like the Nameless. Awkward, but admirably so.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Maybe we can't walk the same path, but...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Passphrase, passphrase, respond at once: Why does life slumber?
rows.speaker: "Contact Doll"

rows.text: We did it... He faded first, causing that power to lose control.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: How... did you...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Death comes for us all eventually.
rows.speaker: "Fading Last Words"

rows.text: I'm starting to hate how powerless I am. How I wish that I had some way to comfort you right at this moment. Don't worry. That was all in the past.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What happened to Firefly?
She had almost reached her demise, yet she survived. Her second death hadn't come yet. It would be upon her soon.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What did the Dreammaster do?

He lured a Glamoth Iron Cavalry to face a Stellaron after years of plotting. Though everything Firefly had learned since entering the dream was true, they were only truths that the Dreammaster wanted her to see.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: And that... is often regarded as the highest form of deception.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The Stellaron answered Firefly's desire to keep living. In response, it recreated within the sweet dream the Swarm Disaster... and the Aeon Ena.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: ...The Swarm Disaster?
It was confined within the dream. Even a Stellaron could not truly revive the Swarm Disaster. The Dreammaster's actions could only evoke fear in those already dreaming.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Yet this Swarm was frighteningly real when you considered the next steps of his plan... Ena's Dream had enveloped the entire star system, which meant the Swarm Disaster would gradually become indistinguishable from reality.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The Propagation would awaken the most primal fears in all dreamers. Through their cries, the Path of Order would be sustained... until the entire cosmos drowned in a singular dream.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I understand you must be confused, and we'll do our best to shed light on the situation. However, before that, it's essential to know that...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I don't think... the goal of the Order was to put everyone into a deep sleep. Quite the contrary — they used the Stellaron to catalyze the leakage of Asdana's memoria into the material world, allowing the Dreamscape to blend with reality.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Me too.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A Memokeeper is looking for them. We must do everything we can as well.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Quite the fateful encounter we have here, friend. Seems you're also a light sleeper. I'll send you some of the IPC's sleep aids one of these days.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Specifically, he's just one step away from becoming an Aeon. The IPC's starships converged here at an opportune moment, and the power of the Preservation seeped into the sweet dream to prevent him from completely ascending. However, that is only temporary.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The key still lies in Ena's Dream. Fear and sweet dreams... He relies on these two lies to gather the dreamers' "shared wishes." He's still just a "false god" who barely managed to ascend.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Unfortunately, we're still in the first layer, which is Ena's Dream. Although we've regained our sense of self, we're still dreaming... We've only managed to connect our individual dreamscapes, but have not escaped.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Humans' yearning for sweet illusions borders on obsession, leading them to subconsciously resist... the harsh reality.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Ena's Dream is no ordinary matter. Even with Constance and me giving it our all, we could only reach the few of you here. It's impossible to find more help.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: It's too late. Unless another Aeon intervenes... But that would be tantamount to igniting a cosmic war among gods.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But time is of the essence. We must take our fate into our own hands.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: It's not just Penacony. The entire Asdana system is done for.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Quiet down. You're just a kid yourself.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Now. I'll tell you, but don't panic.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: But that still doesn't solve the fundamental problem. What about {RUBY_B#Ena}Sunday{RUBY_E#}? He could wipe out all our efforts with no more than a glance the moment we cross the three dreamscape layers.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Take your time to prepare. Before you head out, may I have a moment alone with you, [Trailblazer]? There's one more thing I need to explain to you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You engaged in a decisive battle with Sunday at the Penacony Grand Theater afterward. He had, without question, become an Emanator at that time after usurping the Harmonious Choir.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But you showed no fear and gave it your all in your fight against him, and you emerged victorious with the help of your allies.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Then do your best to not fail.
rows.speaker: Allies Against the Finality

rows.text: As long as you're not afraid to fall asleep, you'll definitely wake up.
rows.speaker: Allies Against the Finality

rows.text: It's the people who first broke free from the sweet dream. The sleeping and shapeless caught a glimpse of their desires.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I think... that's not entirely true. I wish people could find happiness, but I've been tainted by too much nihilism... Sometimes I can't help but think...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Indeed... Behind the shadow of the Nihility, there must exist the most blazing source of light in the world.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I'm glad. The answer itself doesn't matter. What matters is that you've made a decision.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Only a "name" remains... A person that I "was," and now want to "become."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You're looking right at it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Yet that battle, the setbacks, the victory... was just an illusion woven by Sunday. Ena's Dream had already enveloped the entire Asdana System.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: It was impossible for you to beat Sunday at that time. Ena's Dream was so terrifying that even Memokeepers could not act freely in it.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Fortunately, we sought out Acheron first, and she lent us a helping hand. That allowed us to take action along with {RUBY_B#Black Swan}that quarrelsome "friend" of ours{RUBY_E#} and try waking people one by one.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Indeed. Don't forget that, even within the sweet dream, there were still many people yearning, striving, and pushing forward with all their might.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: At that moment, you, too, would face a similar deathmatch. Being woken up by Black Swan was a watershed moment. Due to the existence of Ena's Dream, your memories from that point onward can no longer be viewed from the same perspective as before.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: This way, darling.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Not another one...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Thank you so much, Black Swan.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Finally, I can breathe a sigh of relief.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: This place is the rift between dream and reality. A place reserved only for those who have awakened from Ena's dream.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Do you remember Sunday's ambitious plan? He intended to harness the power of the Stellaron, the collective will of over 100,000 Oak Family members, and the desires of everyone in Penacony to usurp the Harmony and restore the Order.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Unfortunately, it didn't stop there. From the early days of our journey into Asdana, we were already affected by the Stellaron. That strange Dreamscape where we met... Maybe it was a sign that your thoughts were beginning to drift away.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: People think they are awake, but their spirits have long since stepped into the temple of Order.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: This is what makes Ena's Dream so powerful. In this paradise governed by the Order, everyone indulges in their delightful dreams and lives happily ever after.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I believe what you experienced in the sweet dream, except for that flaw, was real. Only in this way could you reach the destination, lifting the crisis in Penacony and embarking on your next trailblazing expedition.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Ena's Dream, the eternal high noon...
If it wasn't for Acheron's plan, we might have been trapped in this dream forever.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Well, I'm not as fortunate as she is. Even if I'm a Memokeeper, I was still influenced by the power of the Order and fell into hallucinations.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: However, thanks to your memories, now we still have a chance to turn the tide.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: We still have a chance, though. To make it happen... please, Black Swan, guide us to those with a strong will.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The truth of the Dreamscape runs deeper. We must notify anyone willing to wake up, so we can end the long night together.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Alright, please come with me.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Stay calm...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I bet that even if I don't resist, you'd still...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Time to get down to business, cowboy.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you're okay!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Unfortunately, we need to stay awake right now rather than sleep. We're still nowhere near capable of breaking free from Ena's Dream.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Let me break the bad news first. The enemy we're up against isn't just Sunday anymore, nor is it the Harmonious Choir that he's usurped.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The Dreammaster has awakened the Swarm Disaster within the sweet dream, and cast shadows into the hearts of all dreamers through Ena's Dream. The primal fear taking root in people's hearts had led them to call out to the Order for protection.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The Path of Order is gradually being restored, and this... has transformed Sunday into Ena.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: With the IPC around, the cosmos doesn't need a second "Order".
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But it doesn't make much of a difference for us.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Sunday's true form has broken free from the Dreamscape, becoming as vast as an Aeon. The Asdana system is no more than a plaything in the palm of his hand.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Indeed. Forget about stopping him. We can't even manage to face him again.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: If we can wake people up and break Ena's Dream, Sunday's divinity will fall with it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: But the current sweet dream is extremely complex. Miss Black Swan, could you please explain the rest of it? My memory... isn't the best, after all.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Time is of the essence, so I'll cut to the chase. There are "three layers" to the dreamscape trapping us.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: First, there's Ena's Dream controlled by Sunday. It wove a beautiful illusion for every dreamer, making them flounder in it.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Third, there's the Twelve Hours established by The Family. This layer was the first to merge with reality and is itself an enormous trap.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Forget about winning. We need to cross all three layers of the dreamscape before we can even face Sunday again.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: To destroy it, we must make everyone in Penacony "want to wake up from their dreams."
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: However, to wake up everyone in Penacony and get them to share the same determination... that would be nearly impossible.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But we can't just stay here and do nothing.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is the first step of our plan. With the assistance from the Garden of Recollection, those who possess a strong will, like you, will gradually awaken from the dream. These free wills are the "discord" that will sway Ena's Dream.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: However, awakening a mere handful of individuals is insignificant compared to the vast number of people immersed in the dream. We must find other ways to awaken the free will of millions of people within a short period of time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Looks like the Jade Abacus of Allying Oath will be the only solution.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...No, no need for that.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Keep your once-in-a-lifetime treasure. We don't need to bother the Xianzhou Alliance for such a tiny request. You want thousands of people with unwavering free will? Hah, that's easy...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Just leave it to us Galaxy Rangers.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Do you know what it is, Acheron?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It's the relic I returned to you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Exactly. Its owner must have told you that it's meaningless to anyone other than a Galaxy Ranger, and that it can only fulfill its purpose when returned to its rightful owner.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Because it's a burial artifact, worthy only of a hero who has served the Galaxy Rangers with honor. When its light illuminates the universe, it means the fall of a hero, and in the direction it falls...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Countless meteors will streak across the sky. Those "meteors" are Galaxy Rangers coming from all corners of the Cosmos, driven by a shared purpose, without questioning the cause or counting the cost. Because we abide by a bottom line...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: The shooting stars of The Hunt only descend on the longest night, and with them... comes the dawn.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: We've stayed silent for far too long. Now, it's time to remind all the cowards, oppressors, and villains of the universe of our presence! I'll be the one to ignite the first spark.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: This should be enough to delay his ascension to godhood. As for the foundation of Ena's Dream, it would take an immense power to shake it in an instant.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I think... That shouldn't be too hard.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: So, you're the key in the end, I assume?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Even if it is just a counterfeit god, we'll need an Emanator to step in.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Perhaps it's not about being an Emanator... This is a different "collective wish." I will do everything in my power... to strike down that evil god for you all.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What about the other two dreamscape layers?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's nothing we can do about them. They're even more dangerous.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Unlike our current gathering, the dissipation of Ena's Dream will take time, which will draw {RUBY_B#Ena}Sunday{RUBY_E#}'s attention.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Exactly. Once we enter the next layer of the Dreamscape, we'll be facing an Aeon's strength head-on. But by then, we'll have played all our cards.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: As for beyond the sweet dream, our only hope lies in intervention from other Aeons... But that would be tantamount to igniting a cosmic war among gods.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: In other words, those who only want to survive by playing it safe will die, while those who dare to face death head-on will live. I like that.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Just these few people? Oh well, that'll do.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...A Stellaron Hunter?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: She was at the edge of the Asdana system, but she still got dragged into this mess. Just finding her nearly wiped me out.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Quite a bold investment strategy! Tell me, with such a huge risk, what kind of payoff are we talking about?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The other two layers of the dreamscape will be handled by the Stellaron Hunters.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: One of our associates is searching in the Twelve Hours for {RUBY_B#the child of Order}the other person chosen by the Harmony{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Oh? Miss Robin?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: She broke free from Ena's Dream through her own strength and left behind a "song" for those in slumber.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It's true that some people are born strong, and others are born weak. If the Trailblaze is the target of heroes, then the Harmony will guarantee that the strong help the weak. Only the people of Penacony themselves can be the saviors of their homeland.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Their path of happiness should be forged by themselves. While I may not be a Nameless, I'm willing to instill courage in all those who need it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This includes my brother as well. Ena's Dream... is too cruel for him, and everyone else.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I see... So we were able to wake up thanks to Miss Robin's help. But... The flaws rooted in human nature can't be eradicated overnight. Do you believe that these efforts alone are enough to convince everyone to choose the right path?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I agree with you, Black Swan. That's why the most critical aspect of this plan is not to convince everyone to choose the right path...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...But to inspire them to save themselves.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: They'll stir up something big to help break you free from the Twelve Hours.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: As for the Primordial Dreamscape, SAM is standing by, just waiting for you to break free from Ena's Dream.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: She will die. She will die a second time, facing everything she wants to run away from.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: But her fate will be determined by you. She will help you break through the second layer of the dreamscape. Then she'll fall into Ena's Dream, which hasn't fully dissipated yet.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: If you defeat Sunday and wake her from that dream, then her second death, too, will become nothing but an illusion.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: But if you fail, the dreamscape will ultimately merge completely with reality, and her death will become a fact.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Miss Memokeeper, it's time for a game of recall. I once said something to you lot back in the Oak Dream.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So long as my "trump card" remains unplayed, none will dare see the hand through to the end. And now, it's time to reveal that ace.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Let me point out two mistakes. One of them... is yours.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Having personally been to the heartland of the Dreammaster's plans, wouldn't I have already found a way to inform the IPC? The fleet's deployment was never meant for a direct confrontation.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It was to seed the Preservation's heart into the dream.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The other mistake was Sunday's, and it was a fatal one. He should never have confiscated my Cornerstone. He should have kicked me out right from the start.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's how every gamble with me goes. The moment you sat down at my table... You've already lost.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: A jade-colored light still sleeps deep within the dreamscape, and it does not require the presence of its owner to unleash its powers.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So what? Even the power of the Ten Stonehearts can't rattle an existence already approaching Aeonhood.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: That's why I said the cosmos no longer needs a second Order. The Dreammaster's plan is indeed flawless... However, when faced with the terror of the Swarm Disaster, how is calling for the Preservation any different from calling for the Order?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The release of {RUBY_B#Jade}the Cornerstone{RUBY_E#}'s powers will absorb the dreamers' desires and offer them the Preservation's promise instead, guiding them to cry out these words... All for the Amber Lord!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I will always believe in tomorrow.
Is this the IPC's real goal? To completely take back Penacony on a conceptual Path level?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What, you think I'm also trampling over others' beliefs? Heh. Sorry, but that's exactly what the IPC believes in: Don't question your own ruthlessness. All that matters is profit.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The new Swarm Disaster will end the same way as it ended before. The Hammer Strike will echo throughout Asdana, seizing the Order's powers on the level of Paths to launch our counter-attack, leaving {RUBY_B#Ena}Sunday{RUBY_E#} powerless to interfere with your actions.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But a new Amber Era will not arrive because of that. Today's Hammer Strike is not the wrath of an Aeon, but humanity's battle cry of defiance.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I'll hold my breath and listen for that moment.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Once our plan succeeds, we can strip Sunday of his godhood, but we'll be too drained to join the battle afterward. So...
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: [Trailblazer], I used to wonder about destiny, about where it's heading.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But you can decide its destination at least for today. The bigger the stage, the more you need to be composed when stepping onto it.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: We've always been interested in the Stellaron Hunters. How about we have a chat after all this is over?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...A chat? You're just after my bounty, aren't you? Stay in your lane.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Are you sure you wish to wake up from your dream?
Wake up.
There are still things to do.
Haha! No way I'm just after that! If you're worried about the bounty, how about I add another billion to that number?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Now that our roles are assigned, let's get to our battlefields and pose a grand finale!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Go, [Trailblazer]. You already know what I want to say.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No. I must keep my promise.
Goodbye, Firefly.
That's alright. Take your time to contemplate this moment. Once you feel ready, let's step onto the final stage.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Very well. Now, please close your eyes...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Am I... awake?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It means you're different, unique... You've done something no one has ever done before.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Sorry, Robin, it's just you... I did not wish for you to know this. It's a pity that things have turned out this way.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Within the foundation of law, humanity establishes civilization...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And through Harmony, we obtain Order.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My brother... Did you still bring the Order's sweet dream into our paradise?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Oww, you're still trying to play the family card at this hour? Your brother doesn't exist anymore. As of now, you'd better call THEM... Ena.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Impressive! You really woke up on your own!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You notice that she glances over at you once in a while.
You can't help but wonder... Was her refusal really as determined as she made it appear?
Let me reiterate. If you've had your fill, it'd be wise to leave before it's too late. The music of the Harmony doesn't tolerate discord.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Owwww. Then I'll reiterate as well. I've done my part, and now I'm simply waiting for the fireworks to begin.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Why don't you just cut to the chase?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Time's short, so I'll condense the report. Oho! That even rhymed! I'm so talented~!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: A nosy Cremator left something on you. She wanted to use it to burn down the illusions you received from the sweet dream, allowing you to wake up from Ena's Dream... Buuut it looks like you don't need it anymore.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...Then, how were you able to reach this place?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Well...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: A fool has thousands of faces. It's gonna take a lot to create a sweet dream that can satisfy me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Both you and I... can still stay awake for just a little bit longer.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Just a little bit...?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Honestly, I don't even need to find you, but I am just sooo kind. I've already killed you once to give you a chance to regain your home field advantage.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You're the last "festival host" awake in Penacony. So, do you want to play a round of roulette? The wager will be the entire Planet of Festivities.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Stay where you are! What are you trying to do by showing up in front of me?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's not over yet. What happened next?
I won't stop here.
Well then, I must come clean about my final lie.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I never showed you anyone's memories, not even my own.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: All you've seen is a "script" I came across by chance. It recorded everything that had happened, and using its stimulation, you actually managed to enter the memories from your own perspective and remember everything anew.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What does that mean?
Even though your memories were cremated to ashes, you were able to recall them once more, treasuring them once again in your heart.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The Stellaron Hunters say you are the one who can turn the wheels of time and give it meaning, that you are the one who can alter destiny and make whole what is incomplete.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Come. I want to show you something.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I want you to watch me blow up all of Penacony. Only then can everyone else launch a counterattack and wake up together.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Think about it. Your brother is already a god beyond the heavens. You're not gonna even see him unless you rip open the sky.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Terminus?
Ever heard of the trolley problem? Make your choice. Do you want everyone to go down together, or to have Penacony make a "small sacrifice"?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Why should I trust the words of a Masked Fool?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Don't think that I'm just trolling you. My bombs are hidden all over Penacony. They took a really long time to set up, you know.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: What's the cat doing here?
Teehee~ Maybe I should blow up a few to demonstrate how they look? Lemme see... which ones should I choose...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...Stop.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: What's gonna happen to the dreamers... once the bombs go off?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: They will all die.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I will find everything that was lost.
...Then you know I'd never agree to it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: When it's time to make a sacrifice, reality won't be giving you any choices. Or do you want to replay the old joke about the Harmony treating everyone the same?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: "Life" is never a joke, Fool. There is no such thing as a lesser evil in this world. Evil, just like morality, cannot be measured, nor can it be compared.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Isn't that still the Harmony's same old song and dance? But that suits me just fine. Didn't I already say that this is a round of roulette, not some pyrotechnics show?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Get ready to sing. Be like a bird. If you can make Xipe hear you, then THEY definitely won't allow me to blow everyone to pieces, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: What will you choose now? You can either watch as I blow the entire place up, or you can try to save their lives.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Maybe this will be your last ever performance.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Last ever performance...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...You feeling nervous? I know the feeling. You should feel nervous when going up on such a big stage for the first time.
rows.speaker: Siobhan

rows.text: ...I'm okay. I just remembered something, that's all.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Miss Siobhan... {RUBY_B#Why does life slumber}Why do you think birds fly{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Destiny works in mysterious ways.
...Why're you asking that all of a sudden?
rows.speaker: Siobhan

rows.text: I have a knack for finding beautiful things.
That was my response as well the first time I heard that question... It's what my brother asked me before I left Penacony. I keep finding myself thinking about it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I don't know. I fly when it's time to fly, and I stop when I don't want to fly anymore. There's no reason.
rows.speaker: Siobhan

rows.text: Nervous?
...It seems that your answer is really similar to mine.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You've also asked me "why do I sing." I think I can answer both of these questions in one go.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The answer wasn't what I initially had in mind. Originally, I wanted to sing because of something specific that I experienced...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I want to know our story from the past.
A Stellaron fell onto my homeworld when I was young. Everything I knew was instantly destroyed. We didn't even get a chance to react to it. No matter what we did, it was too late.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But for some reason, my mother chose to hum a song when she tried to comfort me and my brother.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But I've forgotten everything...
Indeed, what the girl once cherished dearly was her appearance that, if not lost, had changed. Yet, her smile never faded, just like when she faced destiny...
I remember that story. Everyone thought that's why you decided to sing.
rows.speaker: Siobhan

rows.text: No... That experience only made me detest singing.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Are you okay?
...Which one?
I've believed for a long time that songs can't change anything when disasters strike... That music is the most useless thing in this world.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I might be extraordinarily talented in singing, and I might feel super happy whenever I sang... But its futility had always made me depressed.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Then, what changed?
rows.speaker: Siobhan

rows.text: I grew up, and I realized that my brother would sometimes hum the same tune as my mother did. And I thought maybe he missed her, but I was too embarrassed to point that out. I tried to comfort him instead.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: However, his answer to me made me realize what I should be singing for...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Obviously, he didn't give me an answer directly, but it got me to think... Maybe some things don't need a reason or meaning at all?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Go and do what must be done, Fool. It's for the sake of Penacony's future... But I won't let anyone get hurt.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Ooh, did you just have a flashback? Now I'm even more excited!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Lemme check one last time. If you were to die, how would you want people to remember your ending?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: "Like a bird, she lived her life, graceful and composed. Now her beak parts slightly with a sigh, as soft as falling feathers." Like it?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Drop the sanctimonious mask. Singing only needs one thing, and that's "sincerity."
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: My brother... Birds born with wings need no reason to soar into the sky.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And those forced to {RUBY_B#unable to wake up}"fall back to earth"{RUBY_E#} don't need anyone's condescending sympathy.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The sky and earth are each other's "proof" and "aspiration"...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: When {RUBY_B#the waking ones}a soaring bird{RUBY_E#} looks down below, it discovers that even after falling, life still holds hope to continue.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And when {RUBY_B#the sleeping ones}a fallen bird{RUBY_E#} looks up to the sky, it discovers that the possibility of soaring once again still exists in this world.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Perhaps they'll never truly understand each other, but what people need isn't understanding. It's showing a little more compassion for the way others choose to live, and when necessary, extending a helping hand...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Even if you become the only star and prevent everyone from soaring into the sky... they will still be inspired by your radiance, flap their wings with all their might, regardless of whether they've been hurt in their fall.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Thus, the Order's sweet dream will eventually fall. O, Triple-Faced God... If I manage to step onto the Path of Harmony, then please extend your hand and shelter those who believe in you.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And if I am a bird destined to fall, doomed to never sing again... Then, while the sound of me hitting the ground may be my last note for the Harmony, it will never be this world's swansong!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: We can't beat them. Let's run away together.
In the name of the {RUBY_B#dreamchasers}sweet dream{RUBY_E#}, the Charmony Festival... Now begins!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Brother, do you... miss home?
rows.speaker: Guileless Girl

rows.text: Even if I do, it's too late.
rows.speaker: Trustful Boy

rows.text: But you're singing the song Mom used to sing...
rows.speaker: Guileless Girl

rows.text: Because... Even if it's too late, we still have the choice to sing whatever we can.
rows.speaker: Trustful Boy

rows.text: You'll be able to see the fireworks.
Welcome to Horizon of Existence...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: This place is one of the thousands of manifestations belonging to {RUBY_B#IX, the Nihility}the sleeping and shapeless{RUBY_E#}, and it's also an exit out of the Nihility for the awake ones.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Let's bid our final farewells here.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Remember your name. I'll be waiting for you at the end.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: If only people could have each other beyond just memories.
rows.speaker: Memokeeper's Wish

rows.text: I want everything this world has to offer, or perhaps I want to find the one existence that can truly please me.
rows.speaker: Greed's Wish

rows.text: I hope that I'll see her again after I die. Then she'll know that I, too, am only human... And all humans will find happiness in the end.
rows.speaker: Gambler's Wish

rows.text: I hope everyone can always reunite with their family, enjoy home-cooked stew, and keep on laughing.
rows.speaker: Cowboy's Wish

rows.text: "Those afflicted with the Entropy Loss Syndrome will experience an irreversible chronic dissolution of their physical form, gradually fading away. You can still run, jump, and talk with others. Everything seems normal, except you're always just a little slower than everyone else..."
"Until the outlines of yourself and the entire world blur into obscurity. You can no longer distinguish reality from dreams, for both have become equally fractured."
She is nearing the end stage of the Entropy Loss, her mind already splintered first.
And as she gradually forgot everything, the story of you was the last to fade.
One day, those who live will all come to understand how they need to think to create their own happiness.
rows.speaker: Mundanite's Wish

rows.text: The dissolution is not yet over. And in this very instant, her mind holds only "one name" and "one wish."
May people embrace each other, and offer their most sincere compliments to whoever they meet!
rows.speaker: Beauty's Wish

rows.text: Our hopes and dreams are in your hands now. Please guide them to witness every sunrise that is yet to come.
rows.speaker: The Wish Entrusted to You

rows.text: Hey, I've read the "script"! Why are you asking me?
rows.speaker: Allies Against the Finality

rows.text: It's not the time to leave your final words yet!
rows.speaker: Trailblazing Companions

rows.text: We all believe in you.
rows.speaker: Trailblazing Companions

rows.text: You need to believe in us too.
rows.speaker: Trailblazing Companions

rows.text: The trailblazing expedition won't end here.
rows.speaker: Trailblazing Companions

rows.text: We'll wake up together.
rows.speaker: Trailblazing Companions

rows.text: Why does life slumber...? We don't know the answer yet, but we're about to awaken from this dream.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Or perhaps, such is the answer itself.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: However, Firefly's eyes never move again. Every spark of life in her eyes has already gone.
Those things were...?
It is too late. You would rather remember her in the way she wished, and in your mind, the ending would be a happy one.
But when she looks back on this day, she will always discover one regret that can never be mended.
It was because they held onto these desires that they could dream. It was because these desires were never fulfilled that they could wake up.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The crowd buzzes with excitement and the fireworks are about to light up the sky...
That the Nihility is a proud and terrifying dream. It's brought forth not by gain or loss, but by the severing of roads, or even... the loss of desire itself.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: And a song comes on the wind...
"♪ Will she be clearer~ ♪♪~ because she is gone forever?"
"♪ The bouquet you gave me~ ♪♪~ can the sound of its petals falling keep me awake always?"
Fulfilling a wish can certainly make people feel the joy of being alive, but if no new wishes ever surfaced again in people's hearts...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Just as every life that edges closer to death fervently approaches the end of the Nihility...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The voice at your ear blurs, then fades into silence...

You recall the fireworks in your memory, where Firefly caught you as you fell from the sky and carried you up into the heavens. At that moment, the words she spoke left a perfect footnote for the story, one belonging to her, and to everyone under the night sky.
And you know that this footnote no longer exists.

The power of Finality is turning back time, and the girl's final regret is within sight. "A beautiful daydream..." The moment to fulfill that promise has come. You can, you will, you must... make it a reality.
We must pursue that primordial light.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Before you go... Would you tell me your wish?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What about your wish?
What happened?
I understand you must be confused, and we'll do our best to shed light on the situation. However, before that, it's essential to know that...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What is this place?
The déjà vu is strong with this scene...
All of this is just a dream?

I don't think... the goal of the Order was to put everyone into a deep sleep. Quite the contrary — they used the Stellaron to catalyze the leakage of Asdana's memoria into the material world, allowing the Dreamscape to blend with reality.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Did I fall asleep on the Express?
I'm now back at the beginning of the story?
It's so great to see you.
Me too.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What about the others?
A Memokeeper is looking for them. We must do everything we can as well.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Quite the fateful encounter we have here, friend. Seems you're also a light sleeper. I'll send you some of the IPC's sleep aids one of these days.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: What? That's possible?

Specifically, he's just one step away from becoming an Aeon. The IPC's starships converged here at an opportune moment, and the power of the Preservation seeped into the sweet dream to prevent him from completely ascending. However, that is only temporary.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The Aeon of Order?
There must be a way to counter him.
The key still lies in Ena's Dream. Fear and sweet dreams... He relies on these two lies to gather the dreamers' "shared wishes." He's still just a "false god" who barely managed to ascend.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: He's got to have a weakness, right?
Have we woken up from the first layer yet?

Unfortunately, we're still in the first layer, which is Ena's Dream. Although we've regained our sense of self, we're still dreaming... We've only managed to connect our individual dreamscapes, but have not escaped.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Is it really that simple?
How do we do that?
Humans' yearning for sweet illusions borders on obsession, leading them to subconsciously resist... the harsh reality.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Reality sure is a force to be reckoned with...
Can't we wait for the others to wake up?
Ena's Dream is no ordinary matter. Even with Constance and me giving it our all, we could only reach the few of you here. It's impossible to find more help.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Won't anyone on the outside notice?
It's too late. Unless another Aeon intervenes... But that would be tantamount to igniting a cosmic war among gods.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But time is of the essence. We must take our fate into our own hands.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Oh, you're here too?
It's not just Penacony. The entire Asdana system is done for.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Minors are not allowed.
Quiet down. You're just a kid yourself.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Is she okay?
Now. I'll tell you, but don't panic.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: What will she do?
I won't let her die.

But that still doesn't solve the fundamental problem. What about {RUBY_B#Ena}Sunday{RUBY_E#}? He could wipe out all our efforts with no more than a glance the moment we cross the three dreamscape layers.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Her dream deserves a better ending.
I'll defeat him!
Take your time to prepare. Before you head out, may I have a moment alone with you, [Trailblazer]? There's one more thing I need to explain to you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I'll wake everyone up!
I will give Penacony a tomorrow!
I will keep trailblazing forward!
What about Firefly's wish?
She is a hunter who treads upon the Finality, destined to sacrifice her own wishes to defy destiny.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: But no matter which path you and she walk... {RUBY_B#Nihility}Death{RUBY_E#} will always be the destined finale and the last reunion.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What happened?
Are you ready? She, too, was here not long ago... You can witness her "resolve" through this.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...Witness how that tiny spark of bug light broke free from the pull of the Nihility.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Who were you in the past?
rows.speaker: SAM (?)

rows.text: All of this is just a dream?
This scenery... am I... dead? Really... dead...?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Death is one step away from here. Step over this place, and you will truly embrace death. Or... you can turn back.
rows.speaker: SAM (?)

rows.text: Tell me, {RUBY_B#who am I}who were you{RUBY_E#} in the past?
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: Glamoth's Iron Cavalry.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And who are you now?
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: A Stellaron Hunter.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Then, who will you become in the future?
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: ...Just an ordinary girl.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Well then, keep walking forward. Death would suit you better.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: Never. I've fought tooth and nail to get where I am today, and this isn't over yet. Even if everything burns to ashes, I won't give up!
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: You should know that's a wish that can never come true.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: It's so great to see you.
What about the others?
You couldn't become an ordinary girl even in "The Last Sweet Dream."
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: ...Why do you think that?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Entangled in The Family's conspiracy, facing the memetic entities' blades head-on, while challenging the resurrected Swarm Disaster alone, armed only with the "script" that can peer into the future...
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: That's more than enough cards stacked against you.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: What? That's possible?
Do you really think that the time you spent with [Trailblazer] proved anything?
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: For an ordinary girl, simple happiness shouldn't just be a matter of chance.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: But who's to say... all of this isn't what an ordinary girl would do?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...What?
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: There must be a way to counter him.
Perhaps the Dreammaster was right. All the past we've left behind has already determined our future.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: All my experiences so far will still make me choose to step into danger when I face it in the future.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But you misunderstood my answer.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I guess it's my fault too, always talking about wanting a normal life... As if the past that shaped me is some heavy burden weighing me down.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Second, there's the Primordial Dreamscape, which includes Dreamflux Reef. The Swarm Disaster is manifesting again in the "Oak Dream" within this layer and is continuously empowering the Order through an endless stream of fear.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Being a Glamoth's Iron Cavalry and having Entropy Loss Syndrome are more than just scars... They are a past that taught me to cherish, urged me to seek, and showed me how to love.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: All the things you listed are quite extraordinary indeed, but I believe...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Have we woken up from the first layer yet?
Any ordinary girl would make the same choice I did... When faced with everything I have faced.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: How do we do that?

Therefore, I carefully selected a moment where [Trailblazer] was completely unguarded, guiding {M#him}{F#her} to uncover the truth {M#himself}{F#herself} to make {M#him}{F#her} regain {M#his}{F#her} consciousness.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: In the darkest moments, ordinary people never need to feel small. After all, they always discover that they've already become something noble and bright.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Indeed. I can't change the outcome or even the process...
rows.speaker: Firefly
