rows.text: But I can decide how to view my destiny.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: This is just an even deeper form of self-deception compared to actually changing the outcome.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: Free will is mere self-deception for most people anyway. But as long as I'm not asking others to do the same, there's no shame in it for me.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Everyone has their own answer as to why life slumbers.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Some will never find their answer.
rows.speaker: Past

rows.text: But no one can take away their chance to keep looking for the answer.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So, I will leave this place, together with you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Even if embracing my former strength means speeding towards my death.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The name I gave myself is "Firefly." I used to think I was similar to a firefly, just a fleeting glimmer of light...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But later, I realized no one would give themselves an unlucky name.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It was also because I thought fireflies were beautiful. Later, someone told me that my eyes don't actually work very well. Otherwise, I would have figured out that those insects aren't beautiful at all.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Beauty... Love... All our feelings stem from the "flaws" we were born with, and that's what makes each of us unique.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Yet I can't help but love these little things.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Even though I'm sensitive to cold and can't stand the night wind, I still go stargazing.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Even though baking cakes is really troublesome, I'll still keep trying, because I love giving them to people who matter to me and seeing those people smile.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I love going around looking for cute dresses, not to show off to others, but because it makes me feel good.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So, I won't mind any flaws anymore. I won't fear any new scars. I'll give it my all to find what I love, and I won't let destiny take them away. So...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Moths don't fly to flames because they yearn for light.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It's about going through the flames, igniting yourself, and burning with the most intense light. My destiny won't fall into darkness. I will...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...light up everything around me!
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: As long as the clock keeps ticking, death comes for us all eventually...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...and life has its time, too.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: If my world always ends up being burned to ashes... Then let it burn.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Can't we wait for the others to wake up?
As long as I can keep burning, then wherever I am will be "Flames," not "Ashes."
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The Order is one of Xipe's aspects, yet the Harmony stands idle at this moment as Ena is being reborn, without any further intervention.... There must be some deeper reason behind this.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Won't anyone on the outside notice?
The Order is one of Xipe's aspects, yet the Harmony stands idle at this moment as Ena is being reborn, without any further intervention.... There must be some deeper reason behind this.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Ena's Dream is no ordinary matter. Even with Constance and me giving it our all, we could only reach the few of you here. It's impossible to find more help.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Order: Dismember.
Actually, I used to envy you. You wouldn't feel pain even though you were born to bring disaster.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But you should be envious of me now.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm unwilling to face death, nor do I want to keep fighting. But when faced with destiny...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I will never run away.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: To live... Is to imagine a future version of yourself, but fate is never fair.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The choices people make are almost completely dictated by their past. No matter how much they try to move forward, there's no guarantee they'll see the future they've imagined.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: It's the same for every Path. The Nihility already "exists" whether you admit it or not, and nothing can ever completely escape from nihility.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Most Paths make people believe that this world is good. That as long as you are willing to "believe," you would gain power because of your belief.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: But that does not apply to the Nihility. The Nihility is absurd and vast, capturing those who were unwilling to blindly believe yet are powerless to fight back.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: It has nothing to do with good... Be it willing or blind, the way people obtain strength from "faith" should come from within, not from being forced to bow their heads.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: This will be a tough journey, [Trailblazer]. Are you still willing to return to the starting point once again?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: In this way, you will reunite in the warmth of the sunlight.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: May death yet end her "Last Dream."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: May you guide people {RUBY_B#Trailblaze}back{RUBY_E#} to the waking {RUBY_B#tomorrow}world{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Wake up. It's time for this dream to end.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Destiny won't let me give you the answer, and the true ending... is too sad. I'd rather you forget about it.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Is she okay?
...Elio?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: This is what I promised to give you... The truth about the Finality.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: This cat is not Elio, but a strand of Terminus's divine corpus.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The Stellaron Hunters described this scene to me, something I've never seen myself: When Terminus ascends to godhood once more, THEY will manifest their thousand-armed divine form, and proclaim...
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: "Now I am become {RUBY_B#time}Finality{RUBY_E#}, lifting the wheel of time, the destroyer of worlds."
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Then, Terminus turned into a pack of black cats, distributing every ounce of THEIR divine power between those creatures. The cats shall depart from the end of the world, going against the river of time, till the moment of the universe's birth.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What you see is one of those cats. As for Elio, he is an even more special existence. Only the Stellaron Hunters know his true identity.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: It will tell you the truth regarding the ending you haven't yet remembered... but you must be prepared.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: What really happened is that Firefly didn't meet with anyone between the fall of The Great Septimus and when she left Penacony... Not even you.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: She knew how tragic her "third death" would be, so she only dared to watch you from afar and hid on her lonesome when she was about to fade away.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But even sad memories are precious. If you can accept farewells with grace, then you'll gain the strength to create reunions.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: When you bid farewell to loved ones, you should cry while they can still hear you. That's the only way they'll know just how many people love them.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: You know, I often wonder if everything I'm doing right now is just a whimsical gift from "destiny." That I haven't really decided anything, but merely being tossed around at its mercy.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But right now? I don't care. Because my joy is real. My sorrow is real.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: And you will be the same. Remember, if you have regrets that must be mended, then shout with all your might from the depths of your heart. Let it be passed to the end of time and make Terminus, who is about to set off, hear your call.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: The fact that you can see this black cat means Terminus is in the process of passing by you. The power of only one black cat cannot change much, but your past is Terminus's future.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: If it remembers your voice and decides to change something in its own future, your past will change accordingly.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I hope we'll meet again. [Trailblazer]... the only one who could ever please me.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: Father... Destruction is not just a single glorious moment, and the same applies to destiny and memories.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: "Only by enkindling the winter wilderness with flames that cross the sky can we make the indestructible manifest once more."
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: "This is the experience from cultivators who had remade the world, and the wondrous creations from those who painted the world."
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: "Sitting among the embers, they drew the morning star, knowing best: That only in times of extreme hunger do the stars begin to turn."
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: I'll defeat him!
Why does life slumber? You {RUBY_B#already found}will eventually{RUBY_E#} find your own answer.
rows.speaker: The Dahlia

rows.text: But... where's Firefly? I haven't seen her anywhere...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer]? How did you know I was here...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm doing okay...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Sorry. I wasn't trying to avoid you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: How did you know about "the promise"? I never mentioned it...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Maybe it's not just mysterious, but also gentle.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What if I fail?
Then do your best to not fail.
rows.speaker: Allies Against the Finality

rows.text: Will we wake up?
As long as you're not afraid to fall asleep, you'll definitely wake up.
rows.speaker: Allies Against the Finality

rows.text: Those things were...?
It's the people who first broke free from the sweet dream. The sleeping and shapeless caught a glimpse of their desires.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: So, after a wish comes true...
I think... that's not entirely true. I wish people could find happiness, but I've been tainted by too much nihilism... Sometimes I can't help but think...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...People would feel nihilistic?
...Then they will gaze upon nihility.
Indeed... Behind the shadow of the Nihility, there must exist the most blazing source of light in the world.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's what the Order's sweet dream is all about.
First, find what I love...
I'm glad. The answer itself doesn't matter. What matters is that you've made a decision.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Then fight tooth and nail to keep it from being taken away...
Even if I lose everything at the end...
I will continue to trailblaze without hesitation.
What about your wish?
Only a "name" remains... A person that I "was," and now want to "become."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What about Firefly's wish?
You're looking right at it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: At the same time: The beginning of the story, and also, the final stage
I don't think I've mentioned it, but I wrote down everything I wanted to do in my journal before coming here. I'm staying here because I want to fulfill the last wish written in it.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I've been quietly following you and watching you from afar for a while, but I still didn't want to disturb you. I hope your dreams... begin with a smile and end with one too.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What's your last wish?
Where do you want to go now?
To see the fireworks, of course. I heard there's this huge airship in Penacony where you can get an absolutely photo-worthy view of the fireworks.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What if I fail?
Will we wake up?
So...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's go watch the fireworks!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It really is the perfect spot... [Trailblazer], you've got great taste.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Either way, thank you. Looks like it hasn't started yet. Let's sit for a while.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I wonder whether everyone feels speechless at times like this.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Maybe it's neither. There's a saying that I always liked.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: When it comes to someone we want to meet, we always imagine the scene before it happens, imagine the words we'll say that would make them smile.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Slowly but surely, all the things we want to say would have already been said before we even met the person.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So, after a wish comes true...

And when we finally meet again, we realize they're even more beautiful than anything we could have imagined... Yet at that moment, we find ourselves at a loss for words to express just how amazing they really are.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...I'm sorry, but I can't tell you. Elio told me that it would lead to a terrible future. If I say even a few words more, you'll die at the next stop.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Then they will gaze upon nihility.
All I can tell you is why our paths crossed again.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Long ago, you promised me that if I could dream, then you would make it a beautiful daydream.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What matters isn't how they've changed, but that you still hold those same genuine feelings for them.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: First, find what I love...
...I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Yeah. Actually... I still haven't experienced one of the three deaths written in the "script."
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I only realized it after Ena's Dream dissipated. I've made a mistake. Being sent to the Dreamflux Reef by "Death" could hardly be called a death at all. That would've been way too easy.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: As for the true three deaths, the first one... I've known its true form for a long time. I can't dream. After I woke up, I would never dream again. In other words, the me that exists in this dream would completely cease to exist.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The second time, I was killed by the Swarm Disaster. I activated my true power and came back from death.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But that power would inevitably lead me to the third death... My symptoms would accelerate uncontrollably until I die of entropy loss.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The dreamscape had already started merging with reality when we arrived in Penacony. I thought I was dreaming, but I was actually also living in waking reality. It was causing my Entropy Loss Syndrome to worsen.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But don't worry. I asked Silver Wolf about it, and she said things won't get that serious in real life. Let's not talk about this anymore.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I just don't want to see you looking sad. This is our most beautiful daydream, and we should see it through with smiles on our faces.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: After all... we never know when we will use up all the moments we have with someone across all space and time.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Hey, [Trailblazer]... could you close your eyes?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: If this is my only chance to dream, then I want you... to see the best version of me.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: As we near the end, let me indulge in a bit of perfectionism.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Just like what I used to do, let's close our eyes and imagine ourselves being together... Even if you can't see me, you'll still know that we've never been far apart.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: (closes eyes)
Don't you dare sneak away.
I won't. I promise to stay as long as I can.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Hmm... let me think... where should we start...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Right. We should start "where everything began," of course.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Right at that Golden Hour, when you came to save me...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That being said, we could also pretend we're strangers who just happened to meet there.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Me... I'm a student traveling to the Golden Hour, and it'd be nice if I had a bit more pocket money... Oh, and when I show up there, I should dress up a little fancier.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And you... You're a student too! But you came here from a really, really distant planet, completely unfamiliar with your surroundings.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Then, a bunch of mean-looking thugs jumped out, trying to pick on you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: When that happens, I'll step up to the plate. Yeah! Let me be the one to save you this time.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: No worries. That's exactly what I'm going to do.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The result doesn't matter, and even the process isn't important. What matters is how we take part in this journey and how we choose to view it.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So, [Trailblazer], grant me one more wish...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Remember how I held you and flew into the sky when we fought against Ena's Dream? Back then, I wasn't sure if I would ever wake up again, but I was happy.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: We were standing shoulder to shoulder once again, fighting against things we believed were "wrong," and we'd do anything for each other.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Still, I have a tiny, selfish wish. I know you won't forget this moment, but when you look back on it, I want it to feel lighter.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Maybe there were no enemies at all. It was all just a prank. And when I carried you up into the heavens, what we saw there wasn't the terrifying Swarm, but rather... the fireworks that I never got to see.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Firefly!?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... Elio said we're destined to head to different finalities, that we can't have a future.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's why you told me that you'll give me a daydream more beautiful than any ending could ever be.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm looking forward to it, but... can we really... not step over that ending together?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm not scared of death... but please, don't let me die alone...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: They say... you're destined to {RUBY_B#transcend}bring about{RUBY_E#} the Finality.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But I believe you'll be there... You definitely will...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Only you can know it and only you can decide. This cosmos certainly doesn't exist solely for you, nor does it flow only under your gaze... But it's forever waiting for you {RUBY_B#to surpass}to save{RUBY_E#} it.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Even so, I'll still be the last thing you forget...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I won't give up, nor will I blame those who do. All I need to do is return their right to make that choice... and return that right to myself as well.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... Fireworks...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: (No. While she might still be able to see it...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hold her hand and fulfill her wish.
The result doesn't matter, and even the process isn't important. What matters is how we take part in this journey and how we choose to view it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'll do everything I promised you.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Am I... still one step too late...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Why...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: But Firefly can't see it anymore...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No... It's not beyond saving...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I can change the course of destiny and make up for what's missing. If the world has set an endpoint for our destiny, then at the very least... it owes Firefly the bouquet she wanted.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Thank you. I'm sure we'll meet again.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Actually, there are some things about you I feel I should tell you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But I don't want to get you into trouble. Sorry.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Oh right. Wasn't Constance's secret stronghold still somewhere in Penacony?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]
